newsitem.title: JAPAN: TEPCO says to award reactor contract to GE, Toshiba.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO says to award reactor contract to GE, Toshiba.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) said on Friday it plans to award a contract to revamp a reactor to a consortium comprising General Electric Co, Toshiba Corp and Hitachi Ltd.

The consortium is to replace a shroud in a 20-year old reactor at TEPCO's Fukushima nuclear power plant, 228 km (143 miles) northeast of Tokyo, with a new one made of durable stainless steel, a TEPCO spokesman said.

A shroud, which is a cylindrical structure set in a boiling water reactor's pressure vessel to regulate the stream of coolant in the vessel, sometimes suffers from cracks after years of exposure to intensive heat.
The electric power utility has already placed an order for the new shroud with Toshiba, the spokesman said.
TEPCO plans to ask the consortium to start work on the 784,000-kilowatt reactor as soon as the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, which oversees the power industry, approves the project.
The same group of firms will also be in charge of replacing the shrouds of three other TEPCO reactors at the same nuclear power plant, planned by 2000.
TEPCO and Toshiba declined to comment on the estimated cost to modify the 784,000 kw reactor but newspaper reports said it would cost more than 10 billion yen.
Other companies involved in the project could not be reached for comment.
